_status: IMPORTED 2026-08-05. Staged in EU/slices/eu-level/, checked, moved here and registered in src/data/index.ts.
_note: First EU slice in the branch's history, and the first EU data in the graph. Deliberately small: two nodes and one edge, every field traceable to a verbatim quote in EU/SEC05_PartA_2026-08-04.md. The _dropped list is five times longer than the slice and is the point — it records eleven relationships that were looked for and not taken, including both of the branch's central negative results (the Annex XI and Annex B chains, which each stop at AGENCY ONLY at the national boundary). These two nodes are currently a DISCONNECTED COMPONENT: one edge between them, zero edges to the other 133 reports. That is the expected state, not a defect — the EU branch has no documented link to the Canada/US corpus yet, and whether one exists is the question the branch was created to answer.
_provenance: URLs follow the pattern eur-lex.europa.eu/budget/data/DB/<year>/en/SEC<nn>.pdf. SEC05 is hash-verified against that URL (sha256 585c28fc…, 894 024 bytes, byte-identical to EU/SEC05.pdf). The pattern is INFERRED for the other ten sections, on three grounds: the eleven local PDFs share the exact filename convention; they were downloaded in one 3-minute batch on 2026-08-03; and their embedded PDF creation timestamps show ten of the eleven produced on 2026-07-08 within a 50-minute window in section order, all at UTC+02:00, i.e. one publisher's production run. One further fetch of any other section would convert this from inference to verified.
_open_questions: DOMAIN GAP — DOWNGRADED 2026-08-05, no longer blocks import. Neither node has a real domain: Research.1.md's Domain union has 17 subject areas and no 'public-finance' or 'budget' value, and these are administrative expenditure (MFF heading 7, 'European Public Administration'), not transfers. Both nodes carry 'fiscal-transfers' as least-wrong, alongside the Canada Health Transfer and Equalization. 'domains' is now inert metadata: still required on every report, consumed by nothing. Extending the union with 'public-administration' is a data-hygiene question for the Research.2/Research.EU merge, not a prerequisite.

URL GRANULARITY: eu-draft-budget's url points at Section V (the document actually opened, per Research.1.md 6), not at the whole Draft Budget. If a directory-level URL is preferred, it is https://eur-lex.europa.eu/budget/data/DB/2027/en/ — unverified.

EDITION vs SERIES: both nodes are modelled as the recurring series, with the 2027 edition named in the description. sna-2008 in the existing corpus is modelled the other way (edition in the title). Confirm which convention wins for annuals.

reports.title: Draft general budget of the European Union
reports.description: The Commission's annual draft of the Union budget, consolidating the statements of estimates drawn up separately by each EU Institution into one instrument. Published in ten numbered sections, one per Institution (Section I Parliament through Section X EEAS). Article 314(1) TFEU, quoted at the head of every section, states that 'each Institution shall [...] draw up estimates of its expenditure for the following financial year. The Commission shall consolidate these estimates in a draft budget, which may contain different estimates.' The same paragraph records that the Commission 'adjusted the estimates of all Institutions', so a section's narrative request and its expenditure table do not agree — a divergence measured at EUR 498 000 for Section V and EUR 4 529 195 for Section VI.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, by treaty. Article 314(1) TFEU: estimates are drawn up 'for the following financial year'. The 2027 edition is the one read.

reports.title: Statement of Estimates of the European Commission
reports.description: The Commission's own annual statement of estimates, one of the inputs Article 314(1) TFEU requires the Commission to consolidate into the draft budget. The 2027 edition is SEC(2026) 250, June 2026, 539 pages, carrying policy highlights, financial programming, figures by MFF heading and section, and a section on nomenclature changes. It is the document that names MFF heading 7 in words — 'European Public Administration' — and its sub-ceiling 'Administrative expenditure of the institutions'.
reports.cadence_note: Annual. The 2027 edition is titled 'For the financial year 2027' and identified as SEC(2026) 250, June 2026.

dependencies.basis: Article 314(1) TFEU, quoted verbatim at the head of every section of the Draft Budget: '[...] each Institution shall [...] draw up estimates of its expenditure for the following financial year. The Commission shall consolidate these estimates in a draft budget, which may contain different estimates.' The same paragraph opens: 'The introduction to the budget request has been provided by each Institution together with the statement of estimate for its respective budget section.' Direction: the Draft Budget is the dependent — it consumes the statements of estimates. Authority accrues at the estimates. Part A record S05-01.

_dropped.edge: Eurostat annual update report / Joint Index -> a named member-state statistical release
_dropped.why: THE BRANCH'S CENTRAL NEGATIVE RESULT, first of two. COM(2025) 736 final, applying Annex XI to the Staff Regulations, names every national input by institution and never by publication: 'Eurostat calculates this index on the basis of price information provided by the Belgian and Luxembourgish authorities'; 'on the basis of information supplied by the ten Member States referred to in Article 1(4) of Annex XI'; 'in agreement with the national statistical bodies'. Three AGENCY ONLYs. Caveat: Annex XI itself was never retrieved (eur-lex.europa.eu is anti-bot gated), so this refutes the operative document, not the rule. Part A: EU/AnnexXI_PartA_2026-08-05.md.

_dropped.edge: ESA 2010 Annex B transmission programme -> a named member-state statistical release
_dropped.why: THE BRANCH'S CENTRAL NEGATIVE RESULT, second of two, and the one that was predicted to go the other way. Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 Article 1(2) describes its own annex as 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. The programme's table overview has four columns — number, subject, deadline, period — and no column for a publication or publisher. Cleanest test: Destatis, describing its own transmission of government accounts, names ten ESA table numbers (Table 2, 6, 7, 801, 9, 11, 25, 26, 27, 28) and not one German publication. Assessed from staged records, not from Annex B as enacted. Part A: EU/AnnexB_assessment_2026-08-05.md.

_dropped.edge: eu-draft-budget -> Eurostat Report of 31 October on the annual update of remuneration and pensions
_dropped.why: A lead, and the best one in the branch. The chain is real and three documents long: the institutions' staff chapters rest on a salary adjustment; the adjustment is set under Annex XI to the Staff Regulations; and Annex XI Article 1 requires a Eurostat report which COM(2025) 736 names in full, dated and annual. It clears all three of Research.1.md 4's conditions from the quote alone. NOT MINTED because no URL for the Eurostat report has been retrieved and Research.1.md 2 requires one. Part A record C736-03.

SEC05 footnote 4 names both with titles, publisher and page numbers — the only place in the section where an external standard is fully cited: 'See ISSAI 300, Fundamental Principles of Performance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 41, and ISSAI 400, Fundamental Principles of Compliance Auditing, INTOSAI, page 28.' Same shape as sna-2008 / imf-bpm6 / ipsas already in the corpus. NOT MINTED because cadence is not stated anywhere in SEC05, so Research.1.md 4's second condition is unmet from this source; establish it from INTOSAI first. Part A record S05-08.

_dropped.edge: ECA annual work programme -> ECA 2026-2030 Strategy
_dropped.why: Documented in SEC05 but neither endpoint has a retrieved URL. The quote is 'Our 2026+ work programme coincides with the first year of the new ECA 2026-2030 Strategy, which calls for us to Target our audits where we add most value. We will therefore focus our work on what we consider to be four strategic areas.' Note the trap: 'coincides with' is Research.1.md 5a language doing no dependency work; the dependency is in the 'which calls for us to ... We will therefore' clause. Part A records S05-06, S05-07.

_dropped.edge: eu-draft-budget mission appropriations -> ECA multi-annual work programming exercise
_dropped.why: SEC05 point 2.2 states the input plainly and with a lag: 'the ECA estimates its needs based on the results of its multi-annual work programming exercise, carried out in October of year n-2.' But the target is an internal exercise, not a publication. The same sentence names the annual work programme, which IS a publication — and the estimate is NOT said to be based on it. Terminus, kind unpublishable. Part A record S05-06.

_dropped.edge: eu-draft-budget salary chapters -> the Commission's budget guidelines
_dropped.why: The input is real, dated and load-bearing, and has no title. SEC05: 'In accordance with the guidelines issued by the Commission, the budget for Members emoluments (Chapter 10) and for the salaries and allowances of permanent and temporary staff (Chapter 12) and other servants (Chapter 14) is based on the following assumptions: an adjustment of salaries and allowances of + 2,2 % as of 1 July 2026; ... + 2,3 % as of 1 July 2027.' The guidelines are footnoted as a letter of 18 December 2025 from Commissioner Serafin and a note of 12 December 2025 from DG BUDG — identified by sender and date, never by title. Research.1.md 7's 'disclosure stops one level short of a title', in pure form. Part A records S05-02, S05-03.

_dropped.edge: eu-draft-budget standard abatement -> the ECA's vacancy rate at January 2026
_dropped.why: A specific unpublished internal figure moving EUR 3.8m of appropriations. SEC05: 'Taking into account the current vacancy rate (in January 2026), the standard abatement in the Draft budget 2027 is set at 2,4 %', applied at Chapter 1 2 (EUR 158 147 000, the largest chapter in the section). Terminus, kind unpublishable, and directly comparable to cra-pd7-accounts and the Fed's FR 2644 already in the corpus. Internally consistent: 2,4 % of 881 posts = 21,14. Part A record S05-14.

_dropped.edge: EESC IT appropriations -> Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2023/2841 (Cybersecurity Regulation)
_dropped.why: The best-evidenced instrument-to-budget-line relationship found in any institutional section: a named act, a quantified target and the institution's own measured shortfall in one provision. SEC06: 'The Cybersecurity Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2023/2841 ... with a long-term indicative target of at least 10% of the total ICT budget. Despite the repeated requests ... only 3.95% of the DIIT budget was allocated'. NOT MINTED for two reasons: a Regulation is published once and amended, which fails Research.1.md 4's cadence condition; and relationship_type is genuinely unclear — the regulation supplies no data, so uses_data_from is wrong, and 'long-term indicative target' is weaker than a method. Flagged, not picked, per Research.1.md 6. Part A record S06-01.

_dropped.edge: EESC members' allowance budget lines -> an price index
_dropped.why: A documented ABSENCE of a formula, which Research.1.md 8 item 1b asks for explicitly. SEC06: the EUR 367 daily allowance 'was updated by the Council on 21 June 2024 with Decision (EU) 2024/1809, the first adjustment in 11 years. This represents a 26.55% increase in the daily allowance compared to 2013.' Frozen eleven years, then adjusted once by a dated instrument, with no index named anywhere in the section. The opposite of an indexed rate, and the EU counterpart to the Canadian escalator material. Part A record S06-02.

_dropped.edge: any institutional budget section -> any named statistical release
_dropped.why: A corpus observation, not a dropped edge. Across SEC05, SEC06 and SEC07 read in full — 114 pages — the strings 'Eurostat', 'HICP', 'consumer price' and 'index' as a standalone word return ZERO hits, while 'indexation' returns 10, 3 and 3 respectively, every one unqualified. Three institutional sections out of three name no statistical release, no price index and no Eurostat product, while budgeting explicitly for indexation. The institutional strand's administrative machinery is documented in detail and its statistical inputs are not named anywhere in it.
